issues.failure_explanation: The paper says block scrambling is 'necessary' to keep the (0,e,d) property, 'a feat not achieved by standard digit-wise scrambling'. This is false. A (0,e,d)-sequence in base b is an equidistribution statement about base-b elementary intervals of the special shape prod [a_j/b^{e_j k_j}, (a_j+1)/b^{e_j k_j}). A digit-wise nested scramble in base b maps each base-b elementary interval bijectively onto another base-b elementary interval of the same level. Point counts in these intervals are therefore preserved, and the (0,e,d) property survives usual scrambling. Section 4 itself applies usual scrambling to the same sequence and uses its net structure with t_u = sum(e_j-1). The real distinction is the size of the gain coefficients, not preservation of the structure.

failure_location.quote: scrambling entire blocks of digits is the natural and necessary way to maintain this structure

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the motivation. Coarse scrambling preserves the (0,e,d)-structure, but so does usual scrambling. The distinguishing benefit is the O(log d) bound on the maximal gain coefficient.
issues.overall_effect: The stated motivation and the first listed contribution (structure-preserving randomization as something unique to coarse scrambling) overclaim. The formal gain-coefficient results are not affected.
issues.title: Claim that only block scrambling can preserve the (0,e,d)-structure is false
issues.why_classification: Only a motivational sentence and contribution wording must change. No theorem, proof or guarantee is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where all $\pi_{\bullet}$ and $\pi_{\bullet\xi_1 \xi_2 \dots \xi_{k-1}}$ are chosen from permutations on $\Zb$ and are mutually independent.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's definition of a nested scramble requires all digit permutations (one per prefix) to be mutually independent. In the (block) affine matrix scramble, the k-th output block is a linear function of the prefix digits plus M_kk xi_k + Delta_k. The permutations attached to different prefixes at level k therefore differ only by prefix-dependent shifts. They share the same M_kk and Delta_k and are not independent. So the lemma contradicts the paper's own definition. Theorem 2.10 and its corollaries are stated for nested scrambles with two-fold uniformity, so their application to the affine scrambles used in Section 5 is not covered as written.

failure_location.quote: is a nested scramble in base $\bsb$ and has two-fold uniformity.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the definition of the scramble class, or restate Theorem 2.10 for scrambles that satisfy only two-fold uniformity. Add a short argument that the variance computation uses only the joint law of pairs of points.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the affine and block affine scrambles fall under the variance formula, Proposition 2.7 and the gain-coefficient analysis is unsupported as stated.
issues.title: Affine (block affine) matrix scramble is not a nested scramble with mutually independent permutations
issues.why_classification: The fix is a definitional adjustment plus a short observation that the standard variance computation uses only pairwise laws. All results and rates survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Take d=1, u={1}, k=0. By (eq:beta), beta_{u,0} = tilde-beta_{u,u,0} - tilde-beta_{u,emptyset,0} = tilde-beta_{u,u,0} - f_emptyset, which has mean zero. Yet tilde-beta_{u,u,0} is a box average of f with mean f_emptyset, so the identity fails unless f_emptyset = 0. In Walsh terms, L_l requires h_j >= 1 for j in u. The union over k' <= k therefore misses indices with some h_j = 0 for j in u, and the appendix claim that it covers all h_j < b^{k_j+1} is wrong. The correct identity must sum over all w subseteq u, including f_emptyset. The proof of Lemma 4.1 invokes the identity with upper index e_j k_j - 1 = -1 when k_j = 0 and j is not in v. There the empty sum is 0, but the corresponding box average is not 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the identity with all lower-order components (sum over w subseteq u and k'_w <= k_w, including f_emptyset). In Lemma 4.1, show that the lower-order terms cancel in the inclusion-exclusion over v, since they do not depend on chi(j in v) for j outside w. Treat the k_j = 0, j not in v boundary explicitly.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix proof and the proof of Lemma 4.1 rest on a false identity. The statement of Lemma 4.1 appears true, but its proof is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Identity (beta2) omits lower-order ANOVA components; appendix proof and Lemma 4.1 proof rely on it
issues.why_classification: A contained, nontrivial corrected identity and a cancellation argument are needed. The lemma and downstream results remain true.

issues.failure_explanation: Take u={j}, k'=(1) and n=b_j=b. Then G_{u,1}(b^2) = 0 by item (ii), since m_{u,u,1} = b^2. But G_{u,1}(b) = 1 by item (i), since m_{u,emptyset,1} = b. So the claimed equality fails. The true relation follows from (eq:Cformula). Since m_{u,v,k'} = b_j m_{u,v,k}, one gets C_{u,v,k'}(n b_j) = b_j C_{u,v,k}(n), hence G_{u,k'}(n b_j) = G_{u,k}(n). The definition of k from k' in the statement is then pointless, which shows that the right side was meant to carry k.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate (iv) as G_{u,k'}(n b_j) = G_{u,k}(n), which follows directly from (eq:Cformula).
issues.overall_effect: Item (iv) is incorrect as written. The cited argument from [OP24gain] proves a different identity. The statement feeds the reduction from general k to k = 0 used in (vii).
issues.title: Theorem 3.3(iv) is false as stated: the right side must use k, not k'
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction to the statement with a short verification. The method, the results and the bounds are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Take u={j}, k=0 and n=1. The left side is G_{u,0}(b_j) = 0 by item (ii), since m_{u,u,0} = b_j. The right side is G_{u,0}(1) = 1 by item (i). The claim also fails for k = (2), n = b: G_{u,2}(b^2) = 1 but G_{u,0}(b) = 0. Iterating the correct scaling relation gives G_{u,k}(n prod_j b_j^{k_j}) = G_{u,0}(n), with exponent k_j on each b_j. The statement omits these exponents.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace n prod b_j by n prod_{j in u} b_j^{k_j}. This follows by iterating the corrected item (iv), or directly from (eq:Cformula).
issues.overall_effect: Item (v) is wrong as stated. The equality sup G_{u,0} = sup G_{u,k} in item (vii) and its use in Corollary cor:maxgain_uk rest on the correct version, not on this statement.
